strings.name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
strings.role: Novelist and essayist · Migration, history and women’s lives
strings.summary: Adichie grew up in Nigeria and continued her education in the United States, connecting different social experiences through writing in English. Purple Hibiscus, Half of a Yellow Sun and Americanah explore family power, the Nigerian–Biafran War and migration. Her essays and talks also address gender, identity and narrative bias. Her work places ordinary emotions within historical and institutional settings; Dream Count in 2025 continued her examination of women’s lives and choices.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1977–January 2026. The bibliography was cross-checked against a university research website updated in October 2026.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Bachelor’s degree, Eastern Connecticut State University; master’s in creative writing, Johns Hopkins University; master’s in African history, Yale University
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: War remembered through fiction
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Half of a Yellow Sun depicts the Nigerian–Biafran War through individual lives and won the 2007 Orange Prize for Fiction.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Migration and race
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Americanah follows Nigerian migrants’ experiences of identity and belonging and won the US National Book Critics Circle Award for fiction.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Ideas for a broad public
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Talks and essays including We Should All Be Feminists brought gender equality and narrative bias into wider public discussion.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Interviewed by UNESCO
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Discussed Dream Count, her writing process and literature’s role in understanding others’ experiences, continuing her public cultural engagement.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes Dream Count
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Released a novel interweaving four women’s lives to examine love, identity, loss and life choices.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Publishes Notes on Grief
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Used the experience of her father’s death to explore grief, family memory and intimate relationships.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes We Should All Be Feminists
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Developed an earlier TEDx talk into a short book on everyday gender expectations and equality.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Publishes Americanah
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Examined race and identity through migration and cross-border relationships. The novel won the National Book Critics Circle Award for fiction.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Delivers The Danger of a Single Story
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Explored how stereotyped narratives restrict understanding of other societies and emphasized the importance of multiple stories and perspectives.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Receives a MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Received support recognizing creative achievement and promise, continuing her work in fiction and public writing.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Publishes Half of a Yellow Sun
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Set relationships against the Nigerian–Biafran War to show the effects of conflict on ordinary lives.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Publishes her first novel, Purple Hibiscus
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Explored power and coming of age within a family, establishing the international beginning of her career as a novelist.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Enugu
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Nigeria and raised in Nsukka; later continued her education and literary work in the United States.
strings.influence.rationale: Works including Half of a Yellow Sun and Americanah, alongside her talks, explore race, migration and gender and expand African women’s literary influence.
